title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Martinez
description: Context: Our cost-optimization autopilot needs better defaults and visibility for common production workloads. This PR bundles three coordinated changes: (1) safer default batching/caching heuristics for the serving runtime that reduce tail latency while improving token-level throughput, (2) a quantization profile registry and selection path so deployments can pick pre-validated quant configs per model/workload, and (3) a small unit-economics CLI and telemetry hook that exposes per-route token cost estimates to the Redwood Optimize pipeline. Motivation: customers repeatedly hit suboptimal defaults for low-latency workloads and then manually tune batching/quant settings. This work reduces manual effort and gives us observable signals to tune the autotuner.

release_notes:
- Add safer default batching and caching heuristics to reduce manual tuning for low-latency workloads.
- Introduce quantization profile registry and selection path (float16/int8 presets).
- Add unit-economics CLI and telemetry hook for per-route cost estimates.
- Docs: new tuning playbook and sample telemetry outputs.
notes: This PR is backwards-compatible with existing configs: defaults are opt-in via 'autotune.enable_defaults=true' for Dedicated and Private customers. We will progressively roll the default on for hosted customers behind a feature flag after monitoring OOB metrics.
backcompat_instructions: No config breaking changes. To opt into new defaults set 'autotune.use_defaults=true' in runtime config or upgrade to the new image and set feature flag via Console.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive batching could increase latency for short queries. Mitigation: safety cap on batch window, per-route override, rollout behind feature flag and canaryed in Dedicated pools.
testing_plan: Unit tests for batching/caching heuristics, quant profile unit tests, integration test combining a small traffic mix. CI runs and a canary deployment validated metrics (p50/p95/p99 and token cost).
